environment.topology: single-host laboratory (docker compose); primary and recovery databases are containers on one machine
environment.disclaimer: Demonstrates the recovery procedure. NOT geographic disaster recovery and NOT evidence of production recovery times.

summary: Primary killed and fenced; standby promoted after confirmation; 17 services re-pointed. Observed RTO 47.8 s, observed RPO 0 s (0 acknowledged writes lost). The platform now runs on the recovery database; failback is pending.

steps.name: Check preconditions: standby is streaming from the primary
steps.detail: streaming, async, 0 bytes behind; 17 application services running

steps.name: 1. Generate representative transactions and record them
2. Start continuous writes (used to measure data loss)
3. Verify standby replication immediately before the failure
4. Simulate loss of the primary database (SIGKILL)
5. Detect the failure and confirm its scope
steps.detail: primary unreachable, standby reachable, 0 services not ready

steps.name: 6. Fence the failed primary so it cannot accept writes again
steps.detail: old primary container is exited, automatic restart disabled

steps.name: 7. Inspect replication progress on the standby
9. Activate services against the recovery database
steps.detail: 17 services recreated with DB_HOST=postgres-dr and ready

steps.name: 10. Validate authentication (identity store recovered)
steps.detail: new login succeeded; authentication and role checks enforced

steps.name: 11. Validate data integrity of recorded transactions
steps.detail: recorded cases and their decision history are intact

steps.name: 12. Validate a core transaction end to end on the recovery site
steps.detail: new application APP-2026-000034 submitted and approved through all stages

steps.name: 14. Verify event replay is idempotent and reconcile unfinished events
steps.detail: outboxes drained; no duplicate instances, tasks, incidents or notifications

evidence.rpo_measurement: None of the 12 writes acknowledged before the failure was lost. Measurement resolution is the 250 ms write interval; asynchronous replication can lose the last moments before a failure.

timing.explanation: Observed RTO = from the kill of the primary to a new application approved end to end on the recovery site. It includes detection, fencing, the (scripted) operator confirmation, promotion and service restart.

evidence.traffic_redirection: Not applicable in this lab: the gateway address is unchanged and services were re-pointed by configuration. In production this step is a DNS / global load balancer change.
next_steps: The old primary is fenced and must be rebuilt as a standby before it is used again.
Run `npm run dr:failback` for a controlled return to the normal topology.

limitations: Primary and recovery databases are containers on one host: no network partition, no site loss, no geographic separation was exercised.
Fencing was simulated by stopping the container and disabling its restart policy. Production fencing needs an independent mechanism (network isolation or power fencing) and quorum.
Replication is asynchronous: writes acknowledged in the last moments before a failure can be lost. This drill detects such loss but, with a local link, it rarely occurs.
The operator confirmation was supplied by a flag in this scripted run; a human decision takes longer and is part of real RTO.
NATS JetStream, MQTT broker state and the analytical lake were not failed over: they stayed up on the same host.
Small synthetic dataset; timings do not predict production.
